content: During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if absolutely necessary, as determined by your healthcare provider. It is important to note that this drug may pass into breast milk, and its effects on a nursing infant are not fully known. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. It is essential to maintain a comprehensive list of all products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). For less severe cases, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. While using this medication, regular laboratory and medical tests, such as skin examinations, may be required to monitor your condition and detect any potential side effects. Ensure that you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, it is crucial to contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. Do not attempt to double up on doses without professional guidance. Different brands of this medication may have specific storage requirements. Refer to the product packaging for detailed instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless explicitly instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed, following local disposal regulations. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or suitable for your specific needs. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your individual health requirements. Ustekinumab is prescribed to treat conditions such as plaque psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, Crohn's disease, and ulcerative colitis. It works by inhibiting specific natural proteins in the body, interleukin-12 and interleukin-23, which are responsible for inflammation associated with these conditions. While ustekinumab does not cure these diseases, it helps to alleviate their symptoms. Before starting ustekinumab, you should undergo a tuberculosis (TB) skin test to check for latent TB, a form of the disease that may not present symptoms. This medication is administered as an injection under the skin, as directed by your doctor. For psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis, the initial two doses are typically given four weeks apart, followed by maintenance doses every 12 weeks. For Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis, the first dose is usually administered intravenously by a healthcare professional, followed by subcutaneous injections every eight weeks. When injecting this medication under the skin, the preferred sites include the upper arms, buttocks, thighs, or abdomen. Avoid shaking the medication. Inspect the liquid for any discoloration or particles before use; if present, do not use the product. Clean the injection site with rubbing alcohol before administering the dose, and rotate injection sites to minimize skin injury. Do not inject into irritated, sore, or infected skin. To reduce bruising, avoid rubbing the injection site after administration. Common side effects may include bruising, itching, pain, redness, swelling, or hardening of the skin at the injection site, which usually resolves within one to two days. Other potential side effects include headache, back pain, or sinus/throat pain. This medication can suppress your immune system, making you more susceptible to infections such as lung, bone/joint, skin, sinus, or bowel/gallbladder infections. It may also impair your ability to fight existing infections. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of infection, such as persistent nausea or vomiting, worsening redness or swelling at the injection site, fever, chills, flu-like symptoms, painful or frequent urination, unusual vaginal discharge, or severe abdominal pain. In rare cases, ustekinumab may cause a potentially fatal condition known as posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES). Additionally, there is a small risk of developing cancer, including skin cancer, associated with this medication. Discuss the risks and benefits of treatment with your doctor. Serious allergic reactions to ustekinumab are rare but possible. This is not an exhaustive list of side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your healthcare provider for guidance. Before using ustekinumab, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you have any allergies, including to latex or natural rubber found in the needle cover of the prefilled syringe. This medication may increase your risk of infections or worsen existing infections. Avoid receiving live vaccines without your doctor's approval, and stay away from individuals who have recently received oral polio or nasal flu vaccines. Do not receive BCG vaccines for one year after completing ustekinumab treatment. Additionally, avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. During pregnancy, ustekinumab should only be used if clearly necessary, as determined by your healthcare provider. It is not fully known whether this drug passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete and personalized information about this medication and your specific health needs.
